curation.notes: Custom high-speed optical trap: dimeric PCDH15 (wild-type and deafness mutant V507D) tethered between a SpyCatcher-coated 1.5 µm glass pedestal bead fixed to the coverslip and a streptavidin-coated 1 µm latex probe bead; a weak 1,064 nm beam (2 mW, 0.007 pN/nm) detects position on a QPD while a Pockels-cell-modulated 852 nm beam (up to 0.3 pN/nm) applies force. Ca2+-dependence of stiffness and unfolding/refolding studied; detailed methods are in the SI (not provided).

laser_wavelength.note: force-producing trap; a separate 1,064 nm beam is used for position sensing

evidence.snippet: The experimenter next activated a second beam of laser light with a wavelength of 852 nm and an intensity controlled by a Pockels cell modulator. This beam served as an optical trap with a stiffness adjustable up to 0.3 mN m−1.

laser_power_at_objective.note: 1,064 nm position-sensing beam at the focal plane, not the force-producing trap

evidence.snippet: With a power of 2 mW at the focal plane, the trapping stiffness of this beam was only 0.007 mN m−1, so it produced a force on the probe of 1 pN or less.
This beam served as an optical trap with a stiffness adjustable up to 0.3 mN m−1.

bead_size.note: probe bead; pedestal bead is 1.5 µm glass

evidence.snippet: the surrounding solution was filled at a low density with spherical latex beads 1 µm in diameter and previously coated with streptavidin molecules.

Using a high-speed optical trap to examine dimeric PCDH15, we find that the protein's mechanical properties are sensitive to Ca2+ and that the molecule exhibits limited unfolding at a physiological Ca2+ concentration.

Each pedestal bore on its surface a small number of PCDH15 constructs that had been secured at their carboxyl termini, which included SpyTag sequences, to SpyCatcher molecules covalently bound to the bead.
